name: story_deeper
summary: An analytical video essay blending talking head commentary with dynamic graphics, motion design, and side-by-side editing breakdowns. The style relies on clean kinetic typography, graphical storytelling curves, and deliberate perspective shifts to explain narrative structure.

captions.notes: Captions are selectively used for emphasis, humor, or disclaimers rather than continuous transcription.

headline.notes: Massive, bold sans-serif text centered or placed across the screen for major thesis terms and graph titles.

callouts.notes: Labels, arrows, and framed comparison boxes illustrate narrative beats and timeline steps.

transitions.notes: Fast hard cuts supported by audio swooshes, frequent punch-ins on punchlines, and split-screen wipes.

end_screen.tone: Direct educational pitch integrating sponsorship seamlessly into storytelling advice.

rules: Cut every 1.5 to 3 seconds to keep high educational momentum.
Use scale punch-ins on the speaker during comedic beats or thesis statements.
Support conceptual explanations with animated charts, timelines, or curve graphs.
Show side-by-side or before-and-after edits with clear version tags.
Pair visual titles with punchy sound effects like thuds or whooshes.
Punch in dynamically on the speaker on dramatic reveals or comedic beats
Anchor theoretical concepts to an evolving full-screen 2D animated diagram
Use side-by-side split screens with tagged headers to compare edit iterations
Isolate punchy emotional reactions with intentional dead-air pauses and text callouts
Support visual claims with relevant archival or stock footage overlays
Incorporate tactile computer UI b-roll to break up continuous monologue
Animate line graphs synchronously with vocal narrative milestones
avoid: Static wide talking-head shots lasting over 4 seconds.
Unmotivated slow transitions like dissolves or fades to black.
Cluttered frames without a dominant focal point.
Never use continuous word-by-word karaoke captions over the entire video
Avoid leaving talking-head footage static for more than 4 seconds without a cut or punch
Avoid fancy 3D transitions like page turns or generic dissolves
Do not display unlabeled multi-cam comparisons
